messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: auth-service high RPS and 5xx spike detected (auth.login) — please acknowledge
emily: acked. I'm seeing a sudden spike from a handful of IP ranges, requests/s to /v1/auth/login ~12k -> 95k in 3m, error rate to 502s 0.4% -> 14%
raj: putting up quick graph: cpu on auth-gateway spiking, token service latency  p95 1.1s -> 6.8s. Could be credential stuffing or a bot farm.
marta: adding WAF team. Any targeted customers impacted?
emily: initial look — 80% of traffic to login is no-email/password combos, payloads look like password stuffing (many different passwords for same set of emails). Top 10 target accounts are noisy.
kevin: support-lead FYI, we should flag high-risk customers. Support: hold on messaging until we know blast radius.
support-lead: noted. Preparing notification draft if needed.
raj: quick mitigation plan proposal: 1) enable strict WAF signature for auth-paths 2) throttle anonymous login rate per IP to 10rps 3) increase captcha enforcement on web-login 4) temp disable passwordless fallback for high-volume origin IPs
emarta: +1. Can we do 1 and 2 quickly? WAF rule rollout should be quick if signature is precise.
emily: deploying a WAF rule now to block obvious bad UA/known proxy lists. Pushing rule id wf-3042 via waf-api: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WAF_TOKEN' https://waf.internal/api/rules -d '{"rule_id":"wf-3042","action":"block","match":{"path":"/v1/auth/login","ua_regex":"(?i)curl|python-requests|node-fetch","asn_in": ["AS12345","AS54321"]}}'
```
emily: rule pushed, starting to see drop in requests from those IPs within 30s.
raj: applying rate-limit override on the auth gateway for unauthenticated POST /v1/auth/login: policy quick-throttle-2026 = 10rps per IP, burst 20. Pushing now via gateway admin: 
```text
PUT /admin/ratelimit HTTP/1.1
Host: gateway.internal
{ "route": "/v1/auth/login", "key": "remote_ip", "limit": 10, "burst": 20 }
```
kevin: are we sure 10rps won't impact legit flows like mobile app retries?
emily: mobile client behavior is lower than 10rps per IP normally; we also have device tokens that bypass. We'll monitor.
security-bot: Alert: parked sessions matching suspicious patterns. Adding blocklist for IPs that exceed 500 attempts in 10m.
raj: added dynamic blocklist entry set-2026-03-15 with 312 IPs, pushing to edge.
marta: can we geo-throttle for the top offending countries while we triage?
emily: enabling geo-throttle: reduce anonymous auth RPS to 2rps for CN/IN/RU sources for next 30m.
kevin: support-lead please prep customer-facing FAQ saying we're investigating login failures and doing targeted mitigations to protect accounts. Keep it vague on specifics.
support-lead: drafting now. Will coordinate with legal for wording re: account protections.
emily: logs snippet — sample failed attempts (sanitized):
```
2026-03-15T21:13:02Z auth.login ip=203.0.113.45 email=user1@example.com pwd=******** status=401 ua="python-requests/2.28"
2026-03-15T21:13:02Z auth.login ip=203.0.113.45 email=user2@example.com pwd=******** status=401 ua="python-requests/2.28"
2026-03-15T21:13:03Z auth.login ip=198.51.100.12 email=user1@example.com pwd=******** status=429 ua="curl/7.68"
```
marta: any alerts from fraud detection?
security-bot: fraud-detector: multiple account lock triggers for same IP ranges, correlated with known proxy ASN.
raj: measuring impact: total login attempts dropped ~62% after WAF+rate limits. Error 5xx gone down to 0.6%. Successful auths for legitimate users slightly reduced (~1.7% drop) — watch support volume.
kevin: timeline / actions note for postmortem: WAF rule wf-3042, rate-limiter quick-throttle-2026, dynamic-blocklist set-2026-03-15, geo-throttle applied. Create ticket RDW-5921 for long-term mitigations: CAPTCHA for suspicious flows, adaptive backoff, per-account lock escalation.
emily: creating RDW-5921 and adding logs + rule ids, plus list of blocked IPs.
support-lead: support queue spike confirmed: login-related tickets x160 in last 20m. Prioritizing known affected customers flagged by emily.
marta: ok team, plan to keep mitigations for 45m and then slowly relax if stable. Postmortem owners: emily (tech), kevin (comms), raj (ops), marta (security).
raj: handing off to next on-call (@marta) in 25m. Current status: traffic back to acceptable levels, mitigations active.
emily: adding runbook note: if we see >20% of login traffic as automated UA or >5k IPs hitting >100 attempts/10m, escalate to SEV1.
marta: acknowledged handoff. Will monitor metrics and revert geo-throttle if false positives rise.
incident-bot: Incident update logged to RDW-5921. Thread closed by emily at 2026-03-15T21:48:30Z (follow-up required).
